messages:
ashley: Quick sync — thinking through the console UX when multiple automatic fallback policies overlap. e.g. quota-based fallback + regional outage + model degrade. who owns the decision in the UI? :thinking:

sam: Can we show a single resolved policy with a reason chain? like "Active fallback: region-fallback (triggered by: outage -> quota-pressure -> model-degrade)". keep it readable.

lee: I like the chain idea. also need clear CTA for operators: 'force primary' vs 'acknowledge & continue with fallback'. otherwise people will flip things randomly.

pete: UX note: show estimated cost/latency delta for each fallback step. engineers want quick heuristics to decide. tiny inline metric: latency + cost change for replacing with model-quantized-v1.

ashley: agreed on CTA + delta. also audit requirement: every automatic switch must create a single audit entry that includes the evaluated triggers and the policy priority resolution. audit-bot should be able to replay decisions.

audit-bot: auto-log created: id=af-20260301-73d, triggers=[region-unavailable, qps-threshold-exceeded], decision=use-model-quantized-v1, resolution_policy=policy-set-B-priority-2. replay available at /console/audit/af-20260301-73d :zap:

olivia: question — if two policies have equal priority, what's tie-breaker? last-updated? explicit owner override? we should not bake in ambiguous heuristics.

sam: Prefer explicit owner override + deterministic fallback: owner override > SLA tier > most-recently-updated. We should surface which policy would have won if override not set.

marco: For the UI microcopy: "Active fallback — reason(s): region outage, quota pressure. Policy selected: policy-set-B (owner: infra). Actions: [Acknowledge] [Override -> select policy] [Open trace]". Keep it 1 line.

lee: Dev-ex also needs a compact playback panel: show the inputs used to compute the decision (metrics window, model availability, routing table snapshot). a link to "replay decision" that runs the same selection logic against stored inputs.

ashley: We need a safe 'dry override' that tests override but doesn't commit — returns simulated impact. small modal: run dry-run which will show expected latency/cost + potential error rate change.

devex-bot: prototype link: https://figma.redwood/flows/fallback-conflict-2026 (mockup v3). comments enabled.

pete: Implementation note: back-end should return an explainable decision object with fields: selected_policy, reason_chain, alternate_candidates[], cost_estimates, trace_id. we'll render that directly. sample: ```{"selected":"policy-B","reasons":["region-outage","qps"],"candidates":[{"id":"policy-A","rank":2}],"cost_delta":"-12%"}```

olivia: +1 on exposing decision object. also add a small 'why not' for candidates so users see why an option lost. reduces support tickets.

ashley: ok next steps: 1) Sam/Olivia draft microcopy and tie-break rules; 2) Lee/Marco wire the compact playback + dry-run modal; 3) Pete add explainable decision API + audit format; 4) I'll schedule a 30m sync after mocks. cc @devex-bot to update the proto. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: noted. creating task INF-7421: "Fallback conflict UX: tie-break, playback, dry-run" assigned to sam, lee, pete. ETA: 2w.

audit-bot: reminder: ensure replayability retention policy set >=30d for auto-fallback decision traces. current retention=14d. raising ops ticket.

sam: marking follow-ups in the figma thread. will ping for review early next week. :eyes:
